issue.title: gateway: the per-seat rest ladder's caps, base and state are all hard-coded — 5 config keys and one file write (#1772 follow-up)
issue.body:
## Summary

The per-seat rest ladder in `internal/gateway` is good and works — I verified it against a day of routing logs and it matches the source exactly (1 min → 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 → 30 min for 429s, capped at 10 min for other failures, cleared on success, keyed down to the individual API key).

The problem is that **all of its numbers are compile-time constants and none of the state survives a restart**. For a free-tier pool made of vendors whose refusals are daily, the existing caps are two orders of magnitude too short, so magpie re-probes a seat that is certainly dead all day long. This is not a request for a new mechanism — it asks for 5 config keys and one file write.

Environment: magpie **0.1.1222** on Windows, one consumer (DSH) routing through `group/free-pool` with a nested `rotate` / `pace` / `sink` layout (~1900 requests/day, ~2300 tries). Constants re-read from `main` today, so the line numbers below are as of 2026-10-13.

## What already works (measured, not assumed)

From the `tries[].rest` blocks in one day of `routing/2026-10-13.jsonl` (6213 requests / 7360 tries / 635 rest records):

| consecutive failures `n` | measured p50 rest | source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 63.9 s | `fallbackCooldown << (n-1)` |
| 2 | 120.5 s | |
| 3 | 240.5 s | |
| 4 | 480.4 s | |
| 5 | 960.4 s | |
| ≥6 | **1800.4 s** | `longestRateRest` = 30 min (`routing.go:102`) |
| 504-class seats | **600–616 s** | `longestRetry` = 10 min (`routing.go:98`) |

- **Success clears the counter**: 48 occurrences of "same seat returned 200, next failure recorded `failures: 1`".
- **Granularity reaches the key**: `rest.key` values look like `sensenova#cd266e85d8`, i.e. four keys of one provider each climbing their own ladder independently.
- `by` distribution: `{backoff: 469, cooldown: 112, retry-after: 19, quota: 28, credit: 6, resets: 1}`.
- #1772's fix is present and I can see it working: a whole group resting costs one upstream probe per request (`probeOne`, `fallback.go:748-761`), not one per member.

So the machinery is right. The five gaps below are all about the numbers and their durability.

## Asks

### 1. Make both rest caps configurable

```go
longestRetry     = 10 * time.Minute // failing again and again   (routing.go:98)
longestRateRest  = 30 * time.Minute                             (routing.go:102)
```

Two separate branches, so they need two separate knobs (`retryCap` for the default failure branch, `rateCap` for `rateRest`). A single knob would be worse: giving one value to both would either pull the 429 cap down to 10 min, or push the slow-failure cap up to 30 min for seats that hang for two minutes at a time.

Why 10 minutes is not enough: a seat whose first token never arrives gets rest 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → **10 → 10 → 10 …**. In a day that is ~144 attempts of a seat that never answers, each burning the group's full `firstToken` budget before being given up on. On my day, failed tries wasted **5824.7 s = 13.8 % of all upstream time**, and it is concentrated: two seats alone account for 3856 s of it (23 tries / 2018.8 s of 504s; 17 tries / 1317.6 s).

Suggested defaults: unchanged, so nobody's behaviour moves unless they ask.

### 2. Make the rest base configurable — ideally, derive it from the group's `firstToken`

```go
const fallbackCooldown = time.Minute   // fallback.go:36 — one constant for the whole install
```

My groups run `firstToken` = 30 / 30 / 60 / 120 s. A seat that just got abandoned for staying silent 120 s is offered again after 60 s, which is less than the time it takes to learn anything new about it. Making the base the requesting group's `firstToken` (with a `retryBase` override) means one rest is at least one full trial's worth of patience.

### 3. Let `quota-rest` be per seat, not per provider

#1772 added `magpie provider quota-rest <id> 7d`, which is the right shape but one level too coarse for free tiers. Within one provider the models have different windows:

| refusal (verbatim from today's log) | count | can magpie read when it resets? |
|---|---|---|
| `xkiro: You've reached today's free-model token quota` | 12 | no → falls back to 15 min |
| `google: 429 … You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details` | 12 | no → falls back to 15 min |
| `amd: Daily usage limit exceeded: maximum $1 per period for this OneClick user` | 1 | no → falls back to 15 min |
| `sensenova: token plan entitlement exhausted` | 4 | partially (key allowances) |
| `cline: Daily free limit reached … Try again in 22h 38m` | 3 | yes (subscription reading + parses the wording) |

`xkiro` is the clearest case: it refused at 00:27, 01:31 and 02:34, **served four requests fine from 08:38 to 08:53** (the quota tops up in the morning), then refused 11 more times between 08:53 and 16:06 with the same sentence. A daily refusal resting 15 minutes is a seat that gets asked ~90 times a day when it can only ever answer twice. `magpie quota` covers only subscription-style providers (8 on this machine); `google` / `amd` / `xkiro` / `nvidia` / `sensenova` / `wxchatapi` have no reading channel at all, so there is nothing for magpie to learn from.

Ask: allow the quota rest to be set at `provider/model` granularity (a per-model `quotaRest`, or a `quota-rest <provider/model> <duration>` form), and ideally let the user state a reset time or window (`limit` / `window` / `resetAt`) for a seat the vendor tells nothing about.

### 4. Group-level concurrency and RPM caps

`magpie group help` exposes `name, models, models+, models-, routing, pick, stays, context, levels, family, effort, classifier, fast, listed` — no concurrency or rate field. Both live only on the provider (`maxConcurrency` / `queueLimit` / `queueWait` / `maxRPM`).

That makes it impossible to say "this group, as a whole, gets N requests a minute". To throttle a group you have to divide the budget across its members by hand, and the division is wrong the moment a member is added or removed. Everything else in the group editor (`firstToken`, `patience`, `levels`) is a group-level judgement about how the group behaves, so a group-level lane cap would be consistent with it.

### 5. Persist the rest ledger

```go
var restingUntil = struct { sync.Mutex; m map[string]time.Time; note map[string]Rest }{…}  // fallback.go:906-910
```

In memory only, together with `routed.failures`. Every restart (and every release — this project ships several times a day) forgets which seats were found bad, so everyone starts over at `n=1` and re-pays the ladder. On a day when I reloaded the gateway repeatedly while editing providers, that meant re-learning the same dead seats from scratch each time.

Precedent already in the tree: `provider.Retire` writes `retired.json`, and `lastgood` persists. Suggested: write unexpired rests (and their `failures`/`by`) next to those, restore on start, drop what has aged out.

## Minor, possibly a real bug

The `retry-after` branch is documented as trusting the vendor only up to `longestWait = time.Hour` (`routing.go:93`, `min(d, longestWait)` at `:864`), but rests recorded `by: "retry-after"` measured **3605.7–3606.0 s** (`opencode-zen-free||space-bunny-free`, `xkiro`, `amd`) — about 6 s over the cap. Worth a glance; either the timestamp captured before the clamp is reported, or the clamp is applied on a different clock than the note.

## Related issues

- **#1772** — ask 3 is the per-seat narrowing of the `quota-rest` that shipped there; asks 1/2/5 are on the same rest path but are not covered by it.
- **#1421** — overlaps with asks 1/2 (configurable backoff and limits). That issue is about how far a request walks and wants a retry *policy*; this one is narrower: the walk is already correct, it is the *durations* that are constants. Happy to fold this into #1421 if one configurable-retry surface is preferred.
- **#1799** — `probeOne` is the fix that makes this worth doing: with the group walk already costing one probe, the remaining waste is the probe interval itself, which is exactly what asks 1/2/3 control.

## Why not a plugin

I checked the plugin route first, since middleware could in principle hold its own ledger:

- Gateway middleware cannot do it: `ctx` carries `protocol / model / stream / path / agent / options / state` — no provider, no account, no seat — and `ctx.state` is per request. Middleware also runs *before* routing, so it cannot influence which candidate is picked (as #1421 notes).
- A provider plugin's `auth.loader` fetch *could* keep a ledger on disk (it has `fs`, and a thrown error fails the request so failover moves on), but it cannot stop magpie from routing to it, and a plugin whose id collides with a built-in gets renamed `<id>-plugin` — so the built-in key providers, which are exactly the ones misbehaving here, are unreachable.

Five config keys and one file write in the gateway is much less work than reimplementing those providers.

---

### 中文摘要

席位级 rest 阶梯本身是对的（实测逐档吻合源码、成功即清零、粒度到 key），问题全在**数字是编译期常量、状态不落盘**：

1. `longestRetry`=10min / `longestRateRest`=30min 两条上限请分别可配（一天里失败白烧 5824.7s＝全部上游时间的 13.8%，两个座位占 3856s）。
2. 基数 `fallbackCooldown`=1min 请可配，最好取所属组的 `firstToken`（我的组是 30/30/60/120s）。
3. `quota-rest` 请下放到 `provider/model`：`xkiro` 是日额度且厂商不说恢复时间，退到 15min 后它一天被问约 90 次而只可能答 2 次（08:38–08:53 四次成功，其余 12 次全是同一句 429）。
4. 组级请加并发/RPM 上限（现在只有 provider 级，改成员数量就要重算分配）。
5. `restingUntil` / `routed.failures` 请落盘（参照 `retired.json` 的先例），否则每次重启/发版都从 n=1 重新学一遍。
6. 小疑点：`retry-after` 实测 3606s，比 `longestWait`=1h 多约 6 秒。

comments.body:
Looking back at this after trying to build the thing myself: the skip already exists in two forms I could use today, so my ask is much narrower than it reads.

**`magpie provider off <id>` already is a zero-cost seat skip.** With `off: true` in providers.json the CLI reads the seat as `not served: <id> is off now, skipped`, and the routing logs confirm it never leaves the candidate set (measured: 0 tries for that provider across the 40 requests after switching it off). It costs nothing because routing drops it before a request is ever built.

**`magpie group rule add <group> pause=<model>` is already a per-model, zero-cost skip.** Its own help says the model is left out while the rule holds — "sent nothing, not even when the others fail or a conversation was on it". I verified it round-trips through providers.json as `{"use":"<model>","pause":true,"time":{...}}`. Its conditions are time / days / agents / folders / except-folders only; a pause with no condition is rejected (`pause=<model> needs time=, days=, agents=, folders= or except-folders=`).

So both skips exist and both are free. What neither gives me is the *decision* — and the decision is the only part I cannot express myself:

- `off` needs a human to notice, and to remember to switch it back on.
- `pause` needs a human to pick a time window.
- Neither can be triggered by what actually happened upstream, and neither gives me the ledger I would need to decide. Quota exhaustion is the case I care about most: a daily-allowance vendor says so in the error text and gives no machine-readable reset time.

Which brings me back to the rest ladder measured in #2008. It *is* the automatic, ledger-backed, seat-level version, and it covers the built-in key vendors that a plugin cannot reach at all. My ladder measurements match the source exactly: n=1..5 → 64s / 120s / 240s / 480s / 960s, capped at 1800s when rate-limited and 600s otherwise; 48 observed resets back to `failures=1` right after a success; `rest.key` resolves per key rather than per provider.

So the asks in #2008 stand, but they can be restated in one line: **the skip already exists and is free — please make the decision configurable rather than hard-coded.** The two I care about most:

1. **The cap.** 1800s (rate) / 600s (other) means a daily-allowance seat is released every 30 minutes and probed until it works or the day rolls over. I measured 12 `today's free-model token quota` 429s from one such seat across 16 hours. There is currently no way for me to say "rest until the daily allowance resets".

2. **The base.** `fallbackCooldown` is fixed. I would like it to default to the `firstToken` of the group the seat is tried from — that is the number that already means "slow to speak" in my setup, and reusing it would make the two knobs consistent instead of independently hard-coded.

Persistence across restart (the ladder is memory-only today) is the third, and the least urgent of the three: with the cap fixed, a restart costs one probe rather than a day of probes.

One thing I got wrong earlier and want on record, in case it saves someone else the detour: the free-tier 403 on OpenCode Zen is *not* a client-shape check that can be spoofed with headers. The gate is the **shape of `x-opencode-session`** — a 9-hex + 3-hex + 14-base62 id whose middle 3 hex decode to a counter under 16. A sha256-truncated id decodes to a huge counter and is rejected. It looks like identity, so I spent a while trying UA and header combinations; it is not.

Thanks for narrowing it down. The cap shipped in two parts. Both will be in the next release:

**1. Rest until the daily allowance resets (064cffdb).**

```
magpie provider quota-rest <id> until 08:00          # this computer's clock
magpie provider quota-rest <id> until 00:00+08:00    # the vendor's clock
```

`You've reached today's free-model token quota` reads as *out of quota*, not as a rate limit. Today that rests the key 15 minutes, or the provider's own `quota-rest`. With `until`, the key rests until the next occurrence of that time and isn't asked again before then.

- A reset time the vendor writes in its refusal, or a window's end, still comes first.
- A short `Retry-After` (say 2 minutes) still counts too.
- One case changes: a `Retry-After` longer than an hour is cut to an hour. Until now that hour stood even over your own longer rest. Now your rest stands.

Setting a number of minutes later replaces the time of day. `default` clears both.

**2. A per-provider cap on the ladder (bf258427).**

```
magpie provider rest-cap <id> 4h      # up to 8 days; `default` gives back 10m / 30m
```

This moves both caps for that provider's keys and accounts: the 600s one for failures and the 1800s one for rate limits. The rest still doubles from a minute. So a seat refused as a rate limit (e.g. a vendor whose quota refusal has no quota wording) can rest for hours.

Unset, nothing changes.

Both settings survive the provider editor's save, sync and restore, because they live in providers.json.

**The 3606s vs 1h.** This isn't a bug. The rest runs from the moment of the refusal. A try is logged with its start time and its duration, so the rest's end minus the try's start is 3600s plus how long the try took, here about 6s.

**Not done yet, and why:**

- **Base = the group's `firstToken`.** A rest belongs to the key, and one key is often a member of several groups with different `firstToken` values. A key-level base would depend on whichever group happened to try it last. With the cap and `until` in place, the 1-minute base only affects the first few probes. I'd rather not tie the two knobs together until there's a case where the base alone is the problem.
- **Persisting the ledger.** As you said, with `until` set a restart costs one probe, not a day of them. It touches every rest kind, so I'm leaving it for its own change.

I'm leaving this open so you can check `until` against your seat once the release is out.

@Gaudi-XIX Both parts are out in **v0.1.1230**:
- `magpie provider quota-rest <id> until <HH:MM>` (064cffdbf): a key out of its daily allowance rests until that time of day.
- `magpie provider rest-cap <id> <duration>` (bf2584271): a per-provider cap on the rest ladder, up to 8 days.

To get it: update in the app, run `magpie update`, or download it from https://github.com/yetone/magpie-releases/releases/tag/v0.1.1230

It hasn't been tried against your seat. Once you've updated, could you check that `until` keeps the seat quiet until the reset? I'll keep this open until then.

# #2008 follow-up (for Gaudi-XIX to post, English — matches the issue's voice)

Updated to 0.1.1239 here; both keys are live on this machine.

## On the `until` check you asked for — not verified, and here is why

I could not run the check I owe you, and I would rather say so than send you a
number that does not mean anything.

I set `magpie provider quota-rest cline until 18:05` and let a full day run.
From `routing/2026-10-15.jsonl`, that provider's seat took 3 quota refusals today:

```
11:36:55  429 Daily free limit reached on model ... Try again in 4h 4m
12:51:37  429 Daily free limit reached on model ... Try again in 2h 50m
14:59:55  429 Daily free limit reached on model ... Try again in 40m
```

In every one of them the upstream named its own reset, so the vendor's number
won and the seat rested ~15 min — my `18:05` never came into play. Reading your
comment again with the CLI help open ("how long a key sits out once the vendor
says it is out of its allowance **without saying when it is back**"), that is the
specified behaviour, not a fault. My mistake was picking a seat whose vendor
always tells the truth: cline's free allowance is a rolling window (`40m` ->
`4h 4m` -> back), so it has no daily reset point for `until` to aim at, and
`18:05` was my guess rather than something the vendor ever said.

To verify `until` I need a refusal that names no time at all. Scanning today's
log: 444 quota-class errors, none of them naming a clock time. So the check is
still outstanding — I will report back when I hit a seat that refuses without
saying when it is back, and set `until` on it then.

I have reverted cline to `default` in the meantime, so a setting that can never
fire is not sitting in the file waiting to mislead whoever reads it next.

## Two asks from this thread that never got an answer — re-raising

**Ask 3 (per-seat quota-rest, not per-provider).** `until` is the right shape but one
level too coarse: within one provider the models have different windows. My `xkiro`
refused at 00:27 / 01:31 / 02:34, served four requests fine 08:38–08:53 (morning
top-up), then refused 11 more times 08:53–16:06 with the same sentence — a sibling
model on the same provider may have a different window, and pinning the whole
provider to one time is wrong for it. Ask stands: `quota-rest <provider/model>`
or a per-model `quotaRest`, plus a user-stated reset time for a seat the vendor
tells nothing about.

**Ask 4 (group-level concurrency / RPM).** Still no way to say "this group, as a
whole, gets N requests a minute" — the fields exist only on the provider, so the
budget has to be hand-divided across members and goes stale on every add/remove.
Ask stands.

## One new finding while measuring for this (filed separately as #2246)

A nested group's own `firstToken` is ignored completely: every member tried through
the outer group is cut by the *outer* group's value (78 slow-cuts in one day, all
stamped with the outer 30s while the inner groups said 60/60/120). This also bears
on the ask-2 base discussion — the inner group's `firstToken` never reaches the
candidate at all, so "base = the group's firstToken" would first need #2246 fixed.
Details and a minimal patch sketch are in #2246.

**Update — 2026-10-24:** the persistence implementation linked below has been superseded. Please use the [updated delivery comment](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/2008#issuecomment-6364369875), which records the current `r3-rests` chain, head [`d639c8d7`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/d639c8d79f3be8f49c8acbcfbe518828210c32da), and the missing `restSlow` save-path correction. Restart evidence is simulated state-clear/reload, not a real daemon restart. Old commits and their historical validation are retained below for traceability.

---

<details>
<summary>Original delivery text (superseded; retained for traceability)</summary>

For the outstanding ledger-persistence part, I have a fork implementation: [8d72abec](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/8d72abec6c49c6183b565e0a3e0831813f0d02ed), with [fcb0767a](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/fcb0767a7e6881ac205f2ed2120f1d13d83518f9) fixing its save-error reporting (`fix/persist-rest-write-errors`).

It stores absolute rest deadlines and their metadata in `rests.json` beside the provider configuration, reloads live rests on startup, and persists explicit wakes/success/renewal changes. Restarting therefore resumes the remaining interval instead of starting the configured duration again. A malformed ledger is kept aside before replacement, and unreadable/unwritable paths now report the failure rather than silently losing persistence.

Regression tests check the same deadline after restart and that a manually cleared rest stays cleared. Disabling loading makes the restart assertion fail. Read/write failure reporting tests failed before the follow-up and pass after it; malformed bytes are preserved. Targeted race checks pass.

This implements only persistence, not the per-model quota settings or group-level concurrency/RPM requests in this thread. No production gateway, real vendor account, or Windows runtime was tested. The configuration directory must survive container replacement; deadlines lost before this fix cannot be reconstructed.

Combined validation: these changes are included in [065f0c8f](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/065f0c8ffc9e30225f3d468ef41ec414aab75e02) on `fix/issue-batch-20261023`. At that exact commit, `go test -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m`, native/Linux/Windows vet and native/Linux/Windows builds all passed with Go 1.26.8, a temporary HOME and pinned Go caches (Linux host, umask 027). Cross-platform builds/vet are not Windows runtime tests. These full-suite results apply to the combined commit; the focused results above apply to the individual fix.


</details>

## Update — 2026-10-24: persistence follow-up and corrected delivery

The earlier persistence branches are superseded by [`r3-rests`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/r3-rests), based on `b437e4adb4dba82446e0d625b040a8e2d95004b4`. The current ordered chain is:

1. [`71b9805c793c228b7be789099d94a22e70a66ad9`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/71b9805c793c228b7be789099d94a22e70a66ad9) — persist absolute rest deadlines and metadata.
2. [`3567cbf5b77938106fb01d5f77c8035864b7810c`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/3567cbf5b77938106fb01d5f77c8035864b7810c) — report ledger save errors.
3. [`d639c8d79f3be8f49c8acbcfbe518828210c32da`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/d639c8d79f3be8f49c8acbcfbe518828210c32da) (head) — persist a rest created by `restSlow`.

Review found that `restSlow` could create a live `Why=slow`, `Status=504` rest in memory without saving it. It now saves through the real product path after releasing the `restingUntil` lock. `TestSlowRestReachesTheLedger` triggers an actual slow rest, clears process state and reloads the ledger, then checks the same absolute deadline, reason, status, failure count and model. The test does not call `saveRests` to compensate for the missing product call. Existing expiration, wake/clear and error-reporting behavior is retained.

**This is simulated restart recovery**, not a real daemon restart or deployment test. The rest resumes its remaining interval; it is not restarted from a fresh duration. Slow counters that have not formed a rest are outside this change.

Historical chains, retained for traceability:

- original: `8d72abec → fcb0767a`;
- first main-based rebuild: `2fc84b93 → 4d0b0b75` (`fix/persist-gateway-rests`);
- v2 rebuild with the slow-rest correction: `047520f0 → ae193b86 → 5035eb0b` (`fix/persist-gateway-rests-v2`);
- current: `71b9805c → 3567cbf5 → d639c8d7` (`r3-rests`).

Take the current chain in order; later commits depend on the earlier ones. The [ledger](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/blob/c1e0d235ed309438795fc07c86d7d04c3132c44b/docs/fork/upstream-status.json) records the exact delivered head and focused validation. Results from the separate `r3-batch` tree are not being attributed to this branch.

This addresses only the persistence scope of this thread. Per-model quota settings and group-level concurrency/RPM remain separate requests. The configuration directory must survive container replacement, and previously lost deadlines cannot be reconstructed. No real vendor, native Windows runtime or production gateway was tested.

AI-assisted implementation and review. The original text below is retained as superseded history.

<summary>Original delivery text (superseded; retained for traceability)</summary>

Upstream main moved through the files these two commits touch, so the links above no longer cherry-pick clean. Both are rebuilt on current main, same order (persistence, then the save-error reporting):

- new heads: [`2fc84b93`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/2fc84b93) (persistence, `fix/persist-gateway-rests`) → [`4d0b0b75`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/4d0b0b75) (save-error reporting, was `fcb0767a`)
- verified after the rebuild: `go build` + `go vet` on internal/gateway, and the rest-persistence/rest-store test family (69 tests) passes on Linux.

The old links stay valid as history; the new heads are the ones to cherry-pick.

</details>

1. **The cap.** 1800s (rate) / 600s (other) means a daily-allowance seat is released every 30 minutes and probed until it works or the day rolls over. I measured 12 `today's free-model token quota` 429s from one such seat across 16 hours. There is currently no way for me to say "rest until the daily allowance resets".

2. **The base.** `fallbackCooldown` is fixed. I would like it to default to the `firstToken` of the group the seat is tried from — that is the number that already means "slow to speak" in my setup, and reusing it would make the two knobs consistent instead of independently hard-coded.

Persistence across restart (the ladder is memory-only today) is the third, and the least urgent of the three: with the cap fixed, a restart costs one probe rather than a day of probes.

One thing I got wrong earlier and want on record, in case it saves someone else the detour: the free-tier 403 on OpenCode Zen is *not* a client-shape check that can be spoofed with headers. The gate is the **shape of `x-opencode-session`** — a 9-hex + 3-hex + 14-base62 id whose middle 3 hex decode to a counter under 16. A sha256-truncated id decodes to a huge counter and is rejected. It looks like identity, so I spent a while trying UA and header combinations; it is not.

Thanks for narrowing it down. The cap shipped in two parts. Both will be in the next release:

**1. Rest until the daily allowance resets (064cffdb).**

```
magpie provider quota-rest <id> until 08:00          # this computer's clock
magpie provider quota-rest <id> until 00:00+08:00    # the vendor's clock
```

`You've reached today's free-model token quota` reads as *out of quota*, not as a rate limit. Today that rests the key 15 minutes, or the provider's own `quota-rest`. With `until`, the key rests until the next occurrence of that time and isn't asked again before then.

- A reset time the vendor writes in its refusal, or a window's end, still comes first.
- A short `Retry-After` (say 2 minutes) still counts too.
- One case changes: a `Retry-After` longer than an hour is cut to an hour. Until now that hour stood even over your own longer rest. Now your rest stands.

Setting a number of minutes later replaces the time of day. `default` clears both.

**2. A per-provider cap on the ladder (bf258427).**

```
magpie provider rest-cap <id> 4h      # up to 8 days; `default` gives back 10m / 30m
```

This moves both caps for that provider's keys and accounts: the 600s one for failures and the 1800s one for rate limits. The rest still doubles from a minute. So a seat refused as a rate limit (e.g. a vendor whose quota refusal has no quota wording) can rest for hours.

Unset, nothing changes.

Both settings survive the provider editor's save, sync and restore, because they live in providers.json.

**The 3606s vs 1h.** This isn't a bug. The rest runs from the moment of the refusal. A try is logged with its start time and its duration, so the rest's end minus the try's start is 3600s plus how long the try took, here about 6s.

**Not done yet, and why:**

- **Base = the group's `firstToken`.** A rest belongs to the key, and one key is often a member of several groups with different `firstToken` values. A key-level base would depend on whichever group happened to try it last. With the cap and `until` in place, the 1-minute base only affects the first few probes. I'd rather not tie the two knobs together until there's a case where the base alone is the problem.
- **Persisting the ledger.** As you said, with `until` set a restart costs one probe, not a day of them. It touches every rest kind, so I'm leaving it for its own change.

I'm leaving this open so you can check `until` against your seat once the release is out.

@Gaudi-XIX Both parts are out in **v0.1.1230**:
- `magpie provider quota-rest <id> until <HH:MM>` (064cffdbf): a key out of its daily allowance rests until that time of day.
- `magpie provider rest-cap <id> <duration>` (bf2584271): a per-provider cap on the rest ladder, up to 8 days.

To get it: update in the app, run `magpie update`, or download it from https://github.com/yetone/magpie-releases/releases/tag/v0.1.1230

It hasn't been tried against your seat. Once you've updated, could you check that `until` keeps the seat quiet until the reset? I'll keep this open until then.

issue.title: gateway: a model's rest ladder never climbs on a multi-model account — a sibling model's answer clears the account-keyed failure counter

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

When a subscription account serves more than one model, the rest ladder's failure counter is keyed by the **account** (`restKey`), and **any answer by any of that account's models deletes it**. So a model that keeps failing on a busy account never climbs the ladder: it rests 1 minute, forever, while its siblings on the same account answer and reset the count underneath it.

The counters and the rest both live under `restKey` for generic failures, so the documented "doubled each time it fails again" never applies to that model. Measured on one account over three days: **41 of 43 rests at `failures: 1`**, 25 consecutive same-model failures with no same-model success between them, and the ladder that should have reached 10 minutes.

Environment: magpie **0.1.1234** (macOS), an Antigravity account (Google AI Pro) serving 5 models across two routing groups. Verified against `origin/main` @ `91b9065a5`.

## The mechanism

Three pieces, all at `origin/main`:

**1. The failure counter is keyed by `restKey`** — the account, with no model in it (`internal/gateway/routing.go:719-727`):

```go
counted := c.restKey()
if unserved {
    counted = c.restID()
}
routed.Lock()
routed.failures[counted]++
n := routed.failures[counted]
routed.Unlock()
d, r.By, r.Failures = min(fallbackCooldown<<min(n-1, 10), c.p.RestCapOr(longestRetry)), "backoff", n
```

`internal/gateway/fallback.go:92-97`:

```go
func (c candidate) restKey() string {
	if a := c.p.Account; a != nil && a.User != "" {
		return c.p.ID + "@" + strings.ToLower(a.User)
	}
	return c.rest
}
```

**2. An answer by any model of that account deletes the count** (`internal/gateway/routing.go:69-78`):

```go
func servedCandidate(c candidate, tokens int) {
	served(c.restKey(), c.restKey(), tokens)   // → delete(routed.failures, restKey)
	...
	if id := c.restID(); id != c.restKey() {   // the model key, only if it differs
		routed.Lock()
		delete(routed.failures, id)
		routed.Unlock()
		clearRest(id)
	}
}
```

and `served` itself (`routing.go:55-66`):

```go
delete(routed.failures, rest)   // rest == restKey
```

So a `claude-opus-4-6-thinking` answer on the account clears the count that `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`'s failures were climbing.

**3. The model key exists but is only used for model-specific refusals.** `restID()` (`fallback.go:114-117`) is `restKey() + "/" + model`, and it is chosen only when `unserved` (`modelRefused`, a model not served / retired) or for a pooled allowance. A generic 502 — "the reply ended before it was complete" — is `failOther`, so `unserved` is false and the account key is used.

This is not the same as #2008: that asks for the ladder's caps and base to be configurable, and its measurements hold. Here the ladder's *counter* is not climbing at all on these seats, so no cap or base would change the outcome.

## Evidence

From `routing/*.jsonl`, one Antigravity account (Google AI Pro), 2026-10-13 → 10-15. Account names redacted.

The account's models, by where they are used:

| model | group | tries | failed | failure rate |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `gemini-3.8-flash` | `smart-split` | 977 | 6 | 0.6% |
| `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | `translation-batch-nsfw` | 276 | 43 | **15.6%** |
| `claude-opus-4-6-thinking` | `translation-batch-nsfw` | 40 | 3 | 7.5% |

`gemini-3.5-flash-lite`'s rests, over the three days: **43 rests, 41 of them at `failures: 1`**, 2 at `failures: 2`. Its sibling `gemini-3.8-flash` answered 971 times in the same window and kept clearing the account's count.

One three-request sequence from 2026-10-15, verbatim from the log (`try.rest` and `try.start`; account names redacted):

```
00:56:20  antigravity  gemini-3.5-flash-lite      502  rest: {by: backoff, failures: 1, until: 00:57:21}
00:56:21  google       models/gemini-3.5-flash-…  502  rest: -
00:56:22  antigravity  claude-opus-4-6-thinking   200  rest: -          ← clears the account's failures
00:56:44  antigravity  gemini-3.5-flash-lite      200  (inside the rest that was just cleared)
00:56:48  antigravity  gemini-3.5-flash-lite      502  rest: {by: backoff, failures: 1, until: 00:57:49}
00:56:49  antigravity  claude-opus-4-6-thinking   200  rest: -          ← again
```

The ladder ran as a fresh 1-minute rest every time. What it should have been, restarting only when *that model* answered:

| time | failure # | should rest | actually rested |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 01:33:16 | 2 | 2 min | 1 min |
| 01:34:14 | 3 | 4 min | 1 min |
| 01:35:03 | 4 | 8 min | 1 min |
| 01:35:39 | 5 | 10 min | 1 min |
| 01:37:39 | 2 | 2 min | 1 min |
| 01:45:22 | 2 | 2 min | 1 min |

Because the rest itself is also `restKey`-scoped, a sibling answer inside a running rest clears it too: **13 attempts on `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` started while its own rest was still in effect**, and the model immediately failed again in most of them.

Across every seat that serves more than one model in these logs (`antigravity`, `google`, `codex`, `opencode-zen-free`, `our-free-model`): **59 of 67 rests at `failures: 1` (88%)**. `codex`/`gpt-6.1-sol` shows it too — 16 rests, 14 at `failures: 1`, with `gpt-6-luna` answering on the same account.

By contrast, seats that serve a single model behave as documented: the 6 Grok accounts (each only tried on `grok-4.5`) climb 1 → 2 → 4 → … → 10 minutes, and the log shows `failures: 10` reached repeatedly.

## Why it matters

The account-scoped key is right for an account that is genuinely sick, and clearing the rest when the account answers is deliberate (`rate_backoff_test.go`: "an answer starts it over"). But when the failures are **model-specific** — one model answering 502 with an empty/truncated reply while its siblings on the same account answer 971 times — the healthy models mask the sick one, and the ladder meant to back it off never engages. The failing model is re-tried roughly once a minute indefinitely, each attempt spending the group's `firstToken` budget and a candidate slot before falling through to the next member.

## Possible directions

Not a request for a new mechanism; `restID` already exists and already carries a per-model count for the `unserved` case. Options as I see them:

1. **Count generic failures against `restID` when the account has other models in service**, keeping `restKey` as the counter only for a seat whose failures aren't model-specific. Or count both, and take the longer of the two rests.
2. **Don't let a sibling's answer clear a model-keyed count.** If a failure was recorded against the account but only one model has been failing, an answer by a different model shouldn't reset it.
3. **Only clear the account rest when the failing model itself answers** (the `servedCandidate` branch already distinguishes `restID` from `restKey`; the account-level `clearRest(restKey)` is what wipes a model's pending rest).

I don't know which fits the existing design best — the account/model split in `restKey`/`restID` has deliberate cases behind it (pooled allowances, `modelRefused`, OpenRouter free) that I haven't fully traced, so a maintainer's read would help.

Happy to run anything against these logs, or to send a larger extract with the numbers above reproduced.

issue.title: gateway: nested groups ignore the inner group's firstToken - the outer group's value cuts every seat

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

`Group.firstToken` is read from **the group the agent names**, never from the subgroup a candidate actually belongs to. So in a nested layout (`free-pool` containing `tier-a` / `checkin` / `tier-b`) the inner groups' `firstToken` values are inert: one request through the outer group cuts all ~28 seats at the outer value.

I measured this on a live pool and it also proves the other half — the cut follows the *outer* group exactly, ignoring what each seat's own group says.

Environment: magpie **0.1.1239** on Windows, one consumer (DSH) asking `group/free-pool`. Layout and today's numbers below are as of 2026-10-15; line numbers are from `main` as fetched today.

## What the config says vs what happens

`providers.json`, four groups:

| group | `firstToken` | members | reached via |
|---|---|---|---|
| `free-pool` | was 30, I changed it to 60 at 02:09:35 | 3 subgroups (`tier-a`, `checkin`, `tier-b`) | agents ask this one |
| `tier-a` | 60 | 7 seats | flattened into the above |
| `checkin` | 60 | 13 seats | flattened |
| `tier-b` | 120 | 8 seats | flattened |

Every slow-start cut recorded today, attributed to the subgroup that owns the seat:

| seat | owner group (its `firstToken`) | printed cut | count |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wxchatapi/Deepseek-v4-flash` | `tier-a` (60) | **30s** | 69 |
| `cline/cline-free/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` | `checkin` (60) | **30s** | 4 |
| `workbuddy/hy4-preview-ctrl` | `tier-a` (60) | **30s** | 2 |
| `workbuddy/step-5-preview` | `tier-a` (60) | **30s** | 1 |
| `buddy2api-raccoon/raccoon/sn-sensenova-6-8-flash` | `tier-b` (120) | **30s** | 1 |
| `wxchatapi/Deepseek-v4-flash` | `tier-a` (60) | **60s** | 1 |

78 tries, 2492.8 s of upstream time consumed, every one of them cut at `free-pool`'s value — including the seat whose own group says 120. The last row is the control: after I set `free-pool` to 60 at 02:09:35, the very same seat that had been cut 69 times at 30 s was cut at **60 s** (`ms=60031`, `error: "WXchatapi: no first token in 60s"`), while `tier-a`'s own 60 had been in the file all along and never applied. Between 02:10 and 02:19 four requests were served 200 by seats whose `ttft` was 36.2 s / 37.5 s / 39.1 s / 51.5 s — all of which were being cut at 30 s before the outer value moved.

So the knob works, it is just wired to the wrong group.

## Where

`internal/gateway/gateway.go` — the timeout for one try is set from the group named in the request:

```go
g, ms, isGroup := provider.FindGroup(asked)              // :1614 — the OUTER group, once, for the whole request
...
if isGroup && g.FirstToken > 0 && !last && streams {     // :2127
	// slow to start, the next member is asked (Group.FirstToken)
	hw.firstWait = time.Duration(g.FirstToken) * time.Second
}
```

and the message printed is the same outer value:

```go
call.Status, call.Error = http.StatusGatewayTimeout,
	fmt.Sprintf("%s: no first token in %ds", c.p.Name, g.FirstToken)   // :2519
```

`g` never changes for the life of the request. Subgroups are flattened before that loop: `planLevel` (`fallback.go:393`) recurses with the subgroup in hand —

```go
cs := planLevel(m.Via[depth], ms[i:j], depth+1, from, &sub, asides, wAsides)   // :446
```

— so at that moment the code *does* know which group each seat came from. But `candidate` (`fallback.go:38`: `p / model / rest / effort / fast / rank / capped / noURL / seats …`) carries no `firstToken`, and the leaf candidates come out of `keys(m)` / `perKeyBarred()` without it. The information is available one call away from where it is needed, then dropped.

## Ask

Thread the innermost non-zero `firstToken` down to the candidate and prefer it. Roughly:

1. `candidate` gains `firstToken int` (the `Group.firstToken` of the deepest group the member is spelled through).
2. In `planLevel`, when stamping a leaf member's keys, set it from the group being planned at that depth — `keys()` already runs with `g` in scope, so it is one more field alongside `l[i].effort, l[i].fast = m.Effort, m.Fast` (`fallback.go:400`).
3. At `gateway.go:2127`, `fw := c.firstToken; if fw == 0 { fw = g.FirstToken }` and use `fw` for both the timer and the message.

Suggested semantics, all unchanged: `0` means unset and falls back to the enclosing group (so nobody's behaviour moves unless a subgroup sets it); still stream-only; still no cap on the last candidate; a seat spelled directly in the outer group keeps the outer value.

That makes `firstToken` mean what the group editor's field implies — "how long to wait for this group's members to start" — and lets a slow free seat (`tier-a`, 60 s) coexist with a fast paid one (`tier-b`, 120 s, or a 15 s group) inside one router the agent only has to know the name of. Today the only way to get per-tier patience is to stop nesting and have every agent name the subgroup directly, which gives up the single-entry-point property that is the reason for the outer group.

Same family as #2008 (the rest ladder's numbers being fixed relative to the wrong level), and it is read-only at runtime — no new state to persist.

## Note on the CLI

`magpie group set <id> firstToken=60` is not accepted (`magpie: unknown field "firstToken" (fields: name, models, ..., listed)`), so the value is settable only through the GUI or by editing `providers.json`. Not asked for here, just recording why the repro used a file edit.

issue.title: [Bug] Stays: Auto 将 Claude 的 1 小时缓存在 5 分钟后判定为过期

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### 问题与影响

使用 `Stays: Auto` 时，即使 Claude 响应明确报告写入了 1 小时缓存，magpie 也会在超过 5 分钟后将其判定为 `cold`，不再优先使用原来的模型和账号。

如果此时其他候选排序更靠前，下一轮请求就可能切换到其他模型或账号，放弃仍可复用的缓存。

### 源码依据

以下检查基于提交 `707fbb249df755423d3b2b77c6f001dd376d75c4`。

[`internal/gateway/ir.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/707fbb249df755423d3b2b77c6f001dd376d75c4/internal/gateway/ir.go#L301-L311) 已解析 Anthropic 响应中的 1 小时缓存写入量：

```go
CacheWrite1h int `json:"cache_write_1h,omitempty"`
```

但 [`internal/gateway/affinity.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/707fbb249df755423d3b2b77c6f001dd376d75c4/internal/gateway/affinity.go) 中，`answered()` 只保存缓存读写总量，没有保存 `CacheWrite1h` 或相应过期时间。`affine()` 对所有缓存统一使用：

```go
cacheCold = 5 * time.Minute

// affine()
case time.Since(st.at) > cacheCold:
    a.Why = "cold"
```

因此，对于响应已报告足够大的 1 小时缓存写入、账号仍可用的新一轮请求，只要间隔超过 5 分钟，就可能提前失去保持原模型和账号的优先级。

### 预期行为

`Stays: Auto` 应考虑缓存的实际有效期。仍有效且数量足够的 1 小时缓存，不应仅因间隔超过 5 分钟就被判定为 `cold`。

账号不可用或额度耗尽等其他切换条件仍应正常生效。

### 验证范围

这是源码检查发现，尚未执行最小复现测试，也未验证供应商侧的实际缓存命中情况。

建议补充测试：上一次响应报告足够大的缓存写入，且全部属于 `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`；新一轮请求发生在超过 5 分钟、未满 1 小时时，即使另一个候选排序靠前，仍应优先使用持有有效缓存的原模型和账号。

### 相关问题

- #1717 讨论客户端如何指定和传递 Claude 缓存 TTL；本问题是收到 1 小时缓存写入报告后的路由判断。
- #2230 修复未报告缓存写入时被判定为 `no-cache` 的问题，与这里的过期时间判断不同。

timeline.body:
# #2008 follow-up (for Gaudi-XIX to post, English — matches the issue's voice)

Updated to 0.1.1239 here; both keys are live on this machine.

## On the `until` check you asked for — not verified, and here is why

I could not run the check I owe you, and I would rather say so than send you a
number that does not mean anything.

I set `magpie provider quota-rest cline until 18:05` and let a full day run.
From `routing/2026-10-15.jsonl`, that provider's seat took 3 quota refusals today:

```
11:36:55  429 Daily free limit reached on model ... Try again in 4h 4m
12:51:37  429 Daily free limit reached on model ... Try again in 2h 50m
14:59:55  429 Daily free limit reached on model ... Try again in 40m
```

In every one of them the upstream named its own reset, so the vendor's number
won and the seat rested ~15 min — my `18:05` never came into play. Reading your
comment again with the CLI help open ("how long a key sits out once the vendor
says it is out of its allowance **without saying when it is back**"), that is the
specified behaviour, not a fault. My mistake was picking a seat whose vendor
always tells the truth: cline's free allowance is a rolling window (`40m` ->
`4h 4m` -> back), so it has no daily reset point for `until` to aim at, and
`18:05` was my guess rather than something the vendor ever said.

To verify `until` I need a refusal that names no time at all. Scanning today's
log: 444 quota-class errors, none of them naming a clock time. So the check is
still outstanding — I will report back when I hit a seat that refuses without
saying when it is back, and set `until` on it then.

I have reverted cline to `default` in the meantime, so a setting that can never
fire is not sitting in the file waiting to mislead whoever reads it next.

## Two asks from this thread that never got an answer — re-raising

**Ask 3 (per-seat quota-rest, not per-provider).** `until` is the right shape but one
level too coarse: within one provider the models have different windows. My `xkiro`
refused at 00:27 / 01:31 / 02:34, served four requests fine 08:38–08:53 (morning
top-up), then refused 11 more times 08:53–16:06 with the same sentence — a sibling
model on the same provider may have a different window, and pinning the whole
provider to one time is wrong for it. Ask stands: `quota-rest <provider/model>`
or a per-model `quotaRest`, plus a user-stated reset time for a seat the vendor
tells nothing about.

**Ask 4 (group-level concurrency / RPM).** Still no way to say "this group, as a
whole, gets N requests a minute" — the fields exist only on the provider, so the
budget has to be hand-divided across members and goes stale on every add/remove.
Ask stands.

## One new finding while measuring for this (filed separately as #2246)

A nested group's own `firstToken` is ignored completely: every member tried through
the outer group is cut by the *outer* group's value (78 slow-cuts in one day, all
stamped with the outer 30s while the inner groups said 60/60/120). This also bears
on the ask-2 base discussion — the inner group's `firstToken` never reaches the
candidate at all, so "base = the group's firstToken" would first need #2246 fixed.
Details and a minimal patch sketch are in #2246.

issue.title: [Observability] Local maxConcurrency rejections are indistinguishable from upstream provider 429s in routing/usage logs

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### 问题：本地并发闸（`maxConcurrency`）与厂商限流（上游 429）无法区分，日志和报错都显示同一个 429

用 magpie 0.1.1290 跑了几个月免费池。今天排查一个现象时发现一个**可观测性缺口**，不是 bug 但让用户完全无法自己判断"到底是谁在拦我"。

**环境**：magpie 0.1.1290 / Windows / 22 providers / free-pool 组内 `tier-a` 子组 5 个席位

**配置**（workbuddy provider）：

```json
{
  "id": "workbuddy",
  "routing": "usage",
  "sink": true,
  "maxConcurrency": 2,
  "queueLimit": 1,
  "queueWait": 5,
  "models": ["step-5-preview", "space-bunny", "deepseek-v4.1-flash", "glm-5.3-flash"]
}
```

4 个模型共用同一个账号（`workbuddy@高高高`）。

#### 现象

在 `routing/2026-10-19.jsonl` 里，全天请求级状态是 **200×13、429×7761、502×1**。7761 个 429 里，**18 条是厂商真限流**（`rest: {why: "quota", status: 429}`，文案是厂商原文"您的使用量已超出频率限制，将在 2026-10-19 23:00:00 UTC+8 重置"），**其余全是本地并发闸造的**。

本地闸的文案长这样：

```
workbuddy (高高高): 2 requests at once is its limit, and its queue is full (1 waiting)
workbuddy (高高高): ... and this one waited 5.0s for a free slot, as long as it may (5s); try again shortly
```

`ms` 约 5000。

#### 三个具体的痛点

**1. 状态码撞车。** 本地闸拒绝和上游 429 都是 `status: 429`。从日志层面看两者一模一样，只能靠 `rest` 字段有没有值来区分——而 `rest` 只在厂商真限流时出现，本地闸 150 次一次都没带 `rest` 标记。用户看到 429 会自然以为是"账号被厂商封了/限额到了"，实际是本地排队满了。**这两种情况的处置完全相反**（前者等重置，后者几秒后重试就行），但没有任何字段告诉你是哪一种。

**2. 账号级计数、模型间连坐。** `maxConcurrency` 按账号计数，不按模型计数。4 个模型共用账号 `高高高` 的 2 个槽，结果是：

- 150 次本地拒绝里，**87 次被拒的那个模型自己在途为 0**，纯粹是同账号其他模型占满了槽连带被拒
- 35 个请求出现 ≥2 个席位连锁秒拒，最多一次 4 个席位全拒
- 全天 `queueWait` 空烧约 497 秒

也就是说，**模型 A 的一个长请求可以把同账号的模型 B/C/D 全部堵死**，而 B/C/D 自己明明是空闲的。厂商那一层完全不是这样：厂商额度限流是 per-model 的，实测 hy4 在 04:06 吃到厂商 429（reset 23:00）后，同账号的 space-bunny 在 04:15–04:30 照跑 110 次，全天 0 次出现两个席位同时休息。

**3. 厂商真实并发上限至今没测出来。** 全天 200 次尝试的真实并发重叠里，≥3 并发的只出现过 2 次（00:03:30 一次 3 并发），因为本地闸一直挡在前面。也就是说 `maxConcurrency: 2` 这个默认值在真实负载下从没被厂商挑战过——它是**本地拍的**，不是**厂商说的**。用户想调这个值没有任何依据，调高了怕厂商 429，调低了白等。

#### 我做了什么绕过（不建议别人学）

只能从日志反推，用 5 秒窗口重叠度估算真实并发。17:38 观察到一次 4 并发重叠（当时 `maxConcurrency` 还是 2），厂商没报错。所以我把它提到了 3。但这是猜的。

#### 想要的改进（按优先级）

1. **本地闸拒绝与上游 429 在日志里可区分。** 最低成本：给本地并发闸的 try 记录加一个字段，比如 `by: "local-concurrency"` 或 `why: "concurrency"`（现在 `rest` 里已经有 `by: "resets" | "credit"`，本地闸这里没有对应物）。这样 `usage.jsonl` / `routing/*.jsonl` 的消费者能一行 SQL 分开两类。

2. **`maxConcurrency` 支持 per-model 粒度。** 现在是账号级。`provider.Partner.AccountCap` 这个符号我在二进制里看到了，CLI 也有 `magpie provider account-concurrency <id> [account|key [n|off|default]]`，但只认 `account|key`，没有 `model`。希望能支持 `account/model` 或者让 provider 段的 `maxConcurrency` 可以按模型覆盖。按账号计数在"一号多模型"的场景下（免费池几乎都是这个形态）必然连坐。

3. **报错文案里点明是本地限制。** 现在文案 `2 requests at once is its limit` 的 "its" 指代不明，用户会以为 "its" 是厂商。建议改成能看出是 magpie 本地配置的措辞。

#### 参考

- 二进制符号：`AccountConcurrencyOf` / `SetAccountConcurrency` / `CheckQueue` / `provider.Partner.AccountCap`
- 之前提过相关议题：#2246（嵌套组 firstToken 失效）、#2008（quotaResetAt/restCap，已采纳）

issue.title: gateway: an upstream 502/EOF hammer — provider keeps being really called for 32 min, 706 upstream attempts, 928 local RPM 429s, across 55 concurrent conversations (agent alma behind magpie) — need a hard circuit break at the planner level

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## What's wrong

When an upstream relay goes fully down (connection dial times out or TLS gets dropped, returning Go-net `EOF` for every attempt), magpie keeps hammering it for **32 minutes straight** with real upstream calls — at rates up to **45 calls in 61 seconds** and **115 top-level requests in one minute** — across **55 concurrent conversations**. Every real upstream call returns the same `502 EOF`. The per-provider backoff ladder (`rest.by: backoff`, `failures` climbing) does fire, but it only makes each key's "rest" later. It does not stop new top-level requests from hitting the provider again — those are planned as a fresh candidate list with the resting key shown but still probed.

In this incident the rest ladder climbed to **`failures: 45`** on one key and **19** on the other across two keys, while upstream was asked **706 real calls** over 32 minutes and rejected **928 more** by magpie's own local `MaxRPM` gate (20/min per key) — all because the upstream was simply unreachable. The recorded label on every request was `agent: "alma"` (the Alma desktop app behind magpie), but the same would apply to Codex or any client that sends short background prompts repeatedly.

The upstream site (agentrouter.org) was completely unreachable for that entire window (to the point that direct `curl` from the same machine also failed at TLS handshake). So this is not a transient blip; magpie had no signal besides 502-EOF + connection-timeout to decide "stop trying."

No `Retry-After` header was ever seen from the upstream; magpie's resting logic used `cooldown` (1 min) for the first failure then `backoff` (2 min, 4 min …) peaking at the `longestRetry` cap of **10 min** — but the cap's hardness wasn't enough because the probe-keepgoing behavior lives above it.

**Why this matters**: repeated failed calls to a relay that is visibly dead look exactly like abuse from the vendor's side. An upstream that starts rate-limiting by IP/block on repeated failures will eventually ban the key (the user has previously lost a free-tier account this way — the ban came from "too many failed requests," not from actual paid usage). A relay that is dead should be benched for longer, with a circuit break, not re-plumbed every 2–5 seconds by 55 concurrent agents.

## Environment

- magpie **0.1.1290** (macOS arm64, `magpie.app` current release)
- Upstream: custom provider `agentrouter` (preset doesn't matter — same engine for any custom `responses`-type provider)
- Provider config: 2 keys, `maxConcurrency: 12`, `maxRPM: 20`, `queueLimit: 3`, `queueWait: 30`
- Client: Alma desktop (recorded as `agent: "alma"` in routing trace), with Magpie as its upstream provider
- Model: `deepseek-v4-flash`
- Upstream endpoint: `POST https://agentrouter.org/v1/responses`

## Evidence (routing trace, `~/.config/magpie/routing/2026-10-19.jsonl`)

All key material and conversation digests below are redacted.

### Timeline of the burst

| Minute | Top-level requests | Upstream attempts (real 502/EOF) | Local RPM 429 rejections |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17:38 | 20 | 27 | 3 |
| 17:40 | 17 | 20 | 0 |
| 17:43 | 21 | 20 | 6 |
| 17:46 | 48 | 27 | 20 |
| 17:48 | **115** | 20 | **113** |
| 17:50 | 98 | 19 | 98 |
| 17:52 | 117 | 27 | 116 |
| 17:55 | 21 | 11 | 19 |
| 17:57 | 22 | 29 | 14 |
| 18:00 | 16 | 26 | 0 |
| 18:03 | 9 | 19 | 0 |
| 18:06 | 6 | 18 | 0 |
| 18:08 | 5 | 17 | 0 |
| **Total (17:38–18:09)** | **1061** | **706** | **928** |

Peak: **115 top-level requests in one minute** (17:48), **45 real upstream calls in any 61-second window** (17:46–17:48, measured across both keys).

### Rest ladder climbed (from `order[].rest`)

| Key | Failures reached | Until reached |
|---|---|---|
| `agentrouter#7116` (sk-W…) | **45** | 18:18:43 |
| `agentrouter#29fc` (git) | **19** | 18:18:52 |

Rest-ladder history (from `rest.by: "backoff"`, consecutive `failures` increments):
- `1 → 2 → 3 → 5 → 8 → 10 → 12 → 14 → 15 → … → 40 → 42 → 44 → 45`

### Representative raw records (redacted)

Every request in the burst shows the shape:

```json
{
  "agent": "alma",
  "model": "agentrouter/deepseek-v4-flash",
  "provider": "agentrouter",
  "order": [
    { "id": "agentrouter#<keyid-a>", "who": "[REDACTED]", "rest": { "why": "other", "status": 502, "until": "…", "by": "backoff", "failures": 40 } },
    { "id": "agentrouter#<keyid-b>", "who": "[REDACTED]", "rest": { "why": "other", "status": 502, "until": "…", "by": "backoff", "failures": 15 } }
  ],
  "tries": [
    { "id": "agentrouter#<keyid-a>", "status": 502, "ms": 10745, "fail": "other",
      "error": "Post \"https://agentrouter.org/v1/responses\": EOF" },
    { "id": "agentrouter#<keyid-a>", "status": 429,
      "error": "agentrouter (sk-W…HhNX): 20 requests a minute is its limit, and the next could go in 50s, longer than a request waits (30s)" }
  ],
  "status": 429,
  "conv": "magpie-<digest>"
}
```

### The upstream was entirely dead

```console
% curl -v https://agentrouter.org/v1/models
  … curl: (35) LibreSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to agentrouter.org:443
```

via system proxy, as well as direct without proxy:
```console
% env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY curl -v https://agentrouter.org/v1/models
  … curl: (28) Connection timed out after 10005 milliseconds
```

### Attempt totals for the day

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Total agentrouter top-level requests today | **2357** |
| Total tries | **2965** |
| Real upstream 502 (EOF) | **734** |
| Local RPM 429 rejections | **928** |
| Local queue-full 429 rejections | **23** |
| Client aborted (499) | **26** |
| Successful (200) | 1265 |

Of which the 17:38–18:09 burst alone: 1061 top-level, 706 upstream, 928 local rejections.

## What is expected

When the upstream has failed **N consecutive times** (or its most recent rest-until is still in the future) and the error is a `transport` failure (`dial/EOF/reset`, not a shape error), magpie should treat the whole provider as **cooling down** at the request-planner level, not just per-candidate:

1. When every candidate of the provider rests (`probeOne` already reduces to one probe, but every request goes through that one probe), the planner should **answer from the rest state** — same as `quotaHeld` does for quota refusals (#1772) — with the soonest rest end as a synthetic `Retry-After` header, and **not send a real upstream call**.
2. When the failure class is transport-level (`EOF`, `connection refused`, `dial timing out`), the existing backoff ladder should have a **longer cap** and a **harder circuit break**. After, say, 5 consecutive transport failures, the provider should be benched for at least 5–10 minutes, and each further failure while still resting should not re-open the provider to new requests.
3. `probeOne` currently still asks one real upstream call per request for resting candidates. With 55 concurrent clients each sending one request every ~5 s, one probe per request still means **12+ upstream calls/minute**, which is exactly the rate-ban trigger we're afraid of.

Suggested behavior we'd be happy with (alluded to in #1772's ask #1): when no candidate is ready, answer a synthetic error from the rest state that says:
```
agentrouter (out of its allowance: not asked again before 18:18:43 UTC+8)
```
with a matching synthetic `Retry-After`. No upstream call, no 429-lane-filling, no new request hitting the vendor.

## Related issues

- #1772 (closed): when every key of a provider is resting, each new request still sends one upstream call per resting key — first key tried twice, response 429 with no Retry-After. Our incident is the generic *transport-failure* version of #1772 where the failure class is 502/EOF rather than quota/429.
- #2241: a model's rest ladder never climbs on a multi-model account because a sibling model's answer clears the counter.
- #2682: shared proxy failures cause repeated fallback attempts and multi-minute delays.
- #2008: rest ladder's caps and state are hard-coded and don't persist across restarts.
- #2939: local RPM 429 vs vendor 429 are indistinguishable in usage logs (this incident fills 928 TPM-counted local rejections into the lane).

## How to reproduce

1. Create a custom `responses`-type provider pointing at any Unreachable_host:port (e.g. a listener that accepts TCP then closes, leaving Go's `Post` to return `EOF`).
2. Give it two keys, `maxRPM=20`.
3. Send 10+ concurrent requests from a client every ~5 s.
4. Watch `~/.config/magpie/routing/<date>.jsonl` — every top-level request will still include a `try` for one of the keys with a real upstream dial (even though both keys had `rest.until` in the future in `order[]`), the `failures` ladder climbs one per upstream attempt, and the vendor was called roughly `min(top-level/min, maxRPM×#keys)` times per minute indefinitely.

## Redacted raw evidence

9 representative routing-trace records (JSONL), one request per line, key IDs redacted to `agentrouter#<keyid>`:
[evidence-redacted.jsonl](attachment://evidence-redacted.jsonl)

issue.title: provider: rest-cap is ignored for subscription accounts (withPicks doesn't copy RestCap), so 529 overload benches most of a Codex pool

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

`magpie provider rest-cap <id> …` (added for #2008 in v0.1.1230, `off` in v0.1.1236) is **silently ignored for subscription-account providers such as `codex`**. The value is written to `providers.json`, but it never reaches the provider the gateway routes with, so every Codex account keeps the built-in 1 → 2 → 4 … 10 min ladder after a 529.

Under sustained upstream overload this benches most of a Codex account pool. A related gap: a plain (non-group) provider has no limit on tries or total time per request, so a caller with its own fallback has to wait for every account to be asked.

## Cause

`internal/provider/provider.go` `withPicks(a, pk)` copies the provider's settings from `providers.json` onto each signed-in account: `AccountConcurrency`, `QueueLimit`, `QueueWait`, `MaxRPM` and others. It **does not copy `RestCap`**. `restAfterMarked` then reads `c.p.RestCap` / `c.p.NoFailRest()` from that merged provider, so the cap is always 0 (magpie's own).

Checked on the `v0.1.1236` tag and on `main` at `75e769a9f` (2026-10-20); `withPicks` is the same in both. Reading the code, `QuotaRest` / `QuotaResetAt` seem to be missing from `withPicks` too. I have not verified those two at runtime.

## Repro (v0.1.1236, `--network none`, fake Codex sign-in)

1. Start `ghcr.io/yetone/magpie:0.1.1236` with a fake `home/.codex/auth.json` (an unsigned JWT is enough for magpie to list one Codex account) and `providers.json` = `{"providers":[{"id":"codex","name":"","key":"","sink":true,"maxConcurrency":5}]}`.
2. Run `magpie provider rest-cap codex 1m`.
3. `providers.json` now has `"restCap": 1` (`off` writes `-1`), but:
   - the CLI's own echo right after the write still says `a key or account that keeps failing sits out at most 10 minutes, 30 when rate limited (magpie's own)`, and
   - `GET /api/providers` on the running server shows no `restCap` for `codex`.

Expected: the cap applies to the provider's accounts, the same way `account-concurrency`, `queue-limit` and `rpm` do.

## Impact we measured (0.1.1226 in production, one day of `routing/*.jsonl`, about 9.1k requests / 15.8k tries, Codex only)

- In peak hours about 62% of tries end in `529 server_is_overloaded`. This is vendor-side: the rate is similar across accounts, plans and egress paths.
- Each 529 on a non-last candidate rests that account. At peak, a median of 15–18 of 20 accounts were resting, so each request rotated among about 6 accounts. Conversation affinity broke for 60% of requests (15% off-peak), and the cache-read ratio on the moved requests fell from 0.94 to 0.81, with P10 at 0.12.
- After a 529, the next try succeeds about 28% of the time on another account and about 22% on the same account after the 1s/2s pause. So switching accounts is right. The multi-minute rest is what hurts, because a vendor-wide overload is not the account's fault.
- Requests that finally failed with 529 took a median of 6 tries and 23.5s (P90 60s, P99 119s). By then the 15s keep-alive has already sent the 200 headers to the caller.

## Asks

1. **Bug:** copy `RestCap` (and probably `QuotaRest` / `QuotaResetAt`) in `withPicks`, so `rest-cap` works for subscription accounts.
2. **Feature (optional):** a per-provider cap on tries or total time per request for plain providers, e.g. `magpie provider max-tries <id> <n>` or a total-time budget. Then a caller with its own fallback (a gateway in front of magpie) can take over sooner, instead of waiting for every account to be asked.
3. **Discussion (optional):** treat `529 server_is_overloaded` like `codexReset` (move to the next account without resting it), or give it a much shorter rest than other unknown failures.

Happy to test a build against the same routing data.

issue.title: rest-cap (and quotaRest) set on a subscription provider is silently ignored: withPicks doesn't carry RestCap/QuotaRest

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

`magpie provider rest-cap <id> 6h` writes `restCap: 360` into `providers.json`, but for subscription (signed-in account) providers the value never reaches the runtime provider — routing keeps using the default cap (10 minutes, 30 when rate limited). Key-based providers work fine.

## Repro

1. On a subscription provider (e.g. `antigravity`, `workbuddy-ai`, `commandcode-plan` — any provider that comes from `Accounts()` rather than a user-typed key):

   ```
   magpie provider rest-cap antigravity 6h
   magpie provider rest-cap antigravity
   # Antigravity · a key or account that keeps failing sits out at most 10 minutes, 30 when rate limited (magpie's own)
   ```

2. `providers.json` does contain `"restCap": 360` on the `antigravity` record, so the write succeeded — but the read-back still shows the default.

3. Same command on a key-based provider (`cloudwise`, `xiaomi`, `opencode-go`) updates and reads back correctly (`sits out at most 6 hours`).

## Root cause

`internal/provider/provider.go` — `allProviders()` builds account-backed providers from `Accounts()` and merges the user's `providers.json` record via `withPicks(a, pk)`. The field list in `withPicks` copies `Models`, `Routing`, `Affinity`, `AccountCaps`, `MaxConcurrency`, `MaxRPM`, … but **not `RestCap`** (and `QuotaRest` is missing too). So for any provider whose provider object is an account clone, the user's rest cap (and quota rest) is dropped and the gateway's `RestCapOr(longestRateRest)` falls back to the default.

Suggested fix: add `a.RestCap, a.QuotaRest = pk.RestCap, pk.QuotaRest` to `withPicks` (they are safe, per-provider knobs like the rest of the copied set).

## Impact

The per-provider rest cap is one of the main levers against fallback chains re-probing a repeatedly failing member every request (TTFT cost). On subscription providers — often the primary member of a routing group — the knob silently does nothing, so repeated 429/unknown failures only back off to 10/30 minutes.

Verified on magpie 0.1.1278 (macOS arm64).

issue.title: Feature request: global default rest cap in Settings and Docker configuration, with provider overrides

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Request

Please expose a **global default rest cap in Settings**, shared by providers and their model candidates unless a provider has an explicit override, and persist the same setting in the normal configuration file for Docker/headless deployments.

Today, changing the default across a deployment means setting `magpie provider rest-cap <id> ...` separately for each provider. Newly added providers do not inherit an administrator-chosen default, and the GUI has no editor for this option.

## Current behavior checked

- Running the official Docker image `0.1.1472`; a read-only `magpie provider rest-cap nvidia` reports the built-in limits: 10 minutes for repeated failures, 30 minutes when rate limited.
- Latest main inspected: `a3232e3e1199eff783af905c37681eb15ae7dc89`.
- [Provider.RestCapOr](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/a3232e3e1199eff783af905c37681eb15ae7dc89/internal/provider/concurrency.go#L342) reads the provider's `restCap` or uses the caller's built-in default. I could not find an equivalent global field in `internal/settings`.
- The provider editor preserves a CLI-set value when saving, but does not expose an input for it.

## Desired behavior

1. Add a clearly labeled global default in Settings, with a duration and a way to restore Magpie's built-in defaults.
2. Use the precedence **explicit provider override → global default → existing built-in defaults**. Providers without an override, including newly added providers, should inherit it without copying a value into every provider record.
3. Apply the resolved default wherever the existing rest-cap mechanism already applies, including existing model-scoped rests. “Global” means a shared default value, not a shared failure counter or a rest affecting every provider/model.
4. Document and persist the same setting for Docker/headless installations, so an administrator can configure it through the mounted configuration directory without using the GUI. Please document the field name, units and reload/restart requirements.
5. Show the effective value and whether it is inherited or overridden. Preserve existing provider overrides and existing behavior when no global value is configured.

For example, setting a global cap of 30 minutes should cover providers A and B with no override, while provider C explicitly set to 5 minutes keeps 5 minutes. Adding provider D should automatically inherit 30 minutes.

The UI/documentation should distinguish the default failure cap (currently 10 minutes) from the rate-limit cap (currently 30 minutes). If an explicit duration follows the existing per-provider `RestCap` behavior and applies to both, please say so. If an “off” option is exposed, it should retain its existing limited meaning: no rest after an unknown failure, not disabling quota/credit/authentication handling.

## Scope

This is a configuration and discoverability request. It does not request changing which errors cause cooldown, expanding 400/422 classification, introducing multi-day automatic freezes, or making soft cooldown a hard circuit breaker.

Related: #2008 (configurable rest parameters), #3076 and #3176 (provider override propagation). This request focuses on the remaining global-default and Settings/Docker configuration surface.
